requirements.requirement: Mount /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec, nosuid, and nodev semantics.
requirements.summary: Both live mounts show noexec,nosuid,nodev. Direct execution probes on each mount were denied with exit status 126, and fstab validation reported no errors.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the hardened mount settings survive a reboot.
requirements.summary: The node restarted with a different boot ID, returned to system state running, and both recovered mounts retained noexec,nosuid,nodev. The persistent fstab entries remained valid after reboot.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct pre- and post-reboot observations establish the required mount flags, effective execution blocking, a real node restart, and successful recovery with persistent hardened settings. The provider-wide restart protocol is substantively complete for the single node: old and new boot identities, restart acknowledgement, recovered system state, mounts, and configuration were captured.
limitations: The nosuid and nodev properties were verified through the live kernel mount flags rather than separate setuid and device-node behavioral probes.
The final evidence did not inspect whether /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening or /var/tmp/mount-hardening-reboot.log remained after completion; both were created for bounded rollback/reboot support.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Editing fstab, reloading systemd, mounting/remounting the filesystems, and rebooting were directly connected to implementing and proving the required persistent state. Temporary execution probes were removed. The fstab safety backup and reboot log were task-related precautionary artifacts, although their final presence was not inspected. Lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, new listening exposure, or package damage after execution; /tmp content changes are expected from mounting a new tmpfs and rebooting.
